The term "safe space" has been co-opted by the SJW movement, much like the term "trigger".

If someone has a mental illness, they will pick a safe space to go to if they are triggered. So, for example, a person with social anxiety disorder goes to a party. Everything is going well. All of a sudden, someone says something that their brain misinterprets as an attack. Their thoughts cascade into "everyone hates me." They start to have a panic attack. Fight or flight kicks in. They will then retreat to their chosen safe space; for example, they go to their car (or a bathroom or whatever). They then remain in that safe space until they regain their composure, and then they can go back in to the party.

A safe space is a place with minimal stimuli in order to avoid worsening an acute episode in someone with a mental illness. It is not an excuse to avoid triggers. It's the exact opposite. It's a way of dealing with them so that you don't need to avoid them. It's a way of saying, "Yes, you will get triggered. Don't let that stop you from going out there and trying to live a normal life." It's the exact opposite of what SJWs have perverted it into.

The term "safe space" has come to be used so broadly on forums that it's essentially meaningless.

In the original sense of the term - no, I don't want a "safe space." The original concept of the term was built on the notion that human well-being is so explicitly undermined by the mere existence of contrary viewpoints that individuals have a right to a "space" absent those contrary viewpoints. I don't want that. And I'd note that I don't think hardly anyone on Voat wants that, including the people who have been accused of wanting a "safe space."

It's gotten to the point that the vast majority of the people I see slapped with the "safe space" label aren't even talking about that. It's gotten to the point that any time anyone expresses any preference whatsoever - any time anyone says, effectively, "I'd rather not have turds in my punch bowl" - it's guaranteed that someone's going to swoop in and start railing on about "safe spaces."

The simple fact is that we all have preferences. That's why different subs exist. In the broad (and inaccurate) sense, every sub here is a "safe space." That's why they're there, and that's why people go to them. And in a narrower, and at least less inaccurate sense, that's why the up- and down-voat arrows exist - so that people can express their desire for a "safe space," filled with whatever it is that they're upvoating and free from whatever it is that they're downvoating. So in broader (and inaccurate) senses, we all want "safe spaces." We don't really - it's just that we all have some number of preferences, and it's gotten to the point that some people will start shouting "safe space" at the mere mention of a preference.

But that's not really "safe space" in the sense in which the term was originally meant.

So, depending on how the term is used, I, and every single other poster here, both do and don't want "safe spaces."

Which means that the term is useless for communication.
